\difficulty{6}
Let $m$ and $j$ be nonnegative integers with $j\le m$. Let $S$ be a set of coordinates
in a cube of dimension $2m$ and $T$ a set of coordinates in a cube of dimension $2m+3$,
each of cardinality $2j+1$. The Fourier coefficient of majority on the
$(2m+3)$-dimensional cube at $T$ equals $\frac{2(m-j)+1}{2(m+1)}$ times the Fourier
coefficient of majority on the $(2m+1)$-dimensional cube at $S$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.fourierCoeff_majority_next_odd_eq}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b004}
\difficulty{6}
Let $m$ and $j$ be nonnegative integers with $j\le m$. The level-$(2j+1)$ Fourier weight
of majority on the Boolean cube of dimension $2m+3$ equals
$\frac{(2m+3)(2(m-j)+1)}{(2m+2)(2(m-j)+2)}$ times its level-$(2j+1)$ Fourier weight on
the Boolean cube of dimension $2m+1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $m$ and $j$ be nonnegative integers with $j\le m$. The level-$(2j+1)$ Fourier weight
of majority on the Boolean cube of dimension $2m+3$ is strictly less than its
level-$(2j+1)$ Fourier weight on the Boolean cube of dimension $2m+1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $j$, the sequence indexed by nonnegative integers $r$
whose $r$th term is the level-$(2j+1)$ Fourier weight of majority on the Boolean cube of
dimension $2(j+r)+1$ is strictly decreasing.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $k,n_1,n_2$ be natural numbers such that $k>0$, $k$ is odd, $n_1$ and $n_2$ are odd,
$k\le n_1$, and $n_1<n_2$. For majority on the sign cube of dimension $n$, let its
level-$k$ Fourier weight be the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients over all
$k$-element coordinate subsets, with coefficients computed under the uniform measure.
The level-$k$ Fourier weight in dimension $n_2$ is strictly smaller than in dimension
$n_1$.
\end{theorem}
